readmes.signal-board:
# Signal Board

Signal Board is a small workspace app for sharing status, collecting updates, and keeping handoffs clear. It is shaped for teams that want a simple place to coordinate daily work without extra clutter.

## Features
- Create and organize shared status cards
- Review recent updates in one place
- Support a clean flow for team handoffs
- Keep delivery habits steady with built-in checks

## Getting started
Use TypeScript to run the app and connect it to a service endpoint. The project is intended to be started with Node.js and paired with GitHub Actions for repeatable checks. For local work, keep Docker available for a consistent environment, then run the app and verify the main paths before sharing changes.
readmes.taskline-verifier:
# Taskline Verifier

Taskline Verifier is a focused suite for checking important user flows before a release goes out. It is meant to catch regressions early and keep the team confident in everyday changes.

## Features
- Run end-to-end checks for core flows
- Compare expected and actual results with clear reports
- Organize repeatable checks for fast feedback
- Support routine verification during CI/CD

## Getting started
Install dependencies with Node.js, then run the checks from the project folder. The suite works well with GitHub Actions for automated runs and Docker for a stable local setup. Extend the existing cases, execute the full set, and review the report before merging.
readmes.ledger-path:
# Ledger Path

Ledger Path is a compact service for storing budget entries and producing simple monthly summaries. It is designed for a single person or a small group that wants a dependable way to track spending patterns.

## Features
- Add and review income or expense entries
- Produce monthly summaries from stored records
- Keep request handling straightforward and predictable
- Support automated checks for core behavior

## Getting started
Build the service with Java, then run the checks with JUnit. Use Docker for a repeatable local setup, and point the app at PostgreSQL for storage. After that, start the service, submit a few sample entries, and confirm the summary output.
